note: _est autem Hierosolyma super Probatica piscina_ (Weber/Gryson) – there is in Jerusalem near the Probatica (Sheep Gate) a pond; the Clementina does not have the word _super_, which leads to the translation: “there is in Jerusalem the Probaica pond” (making “Probatica” the name of the pond). Meant is: _ad Probaticam portam_ (near the Probatica) _est piscina_. The NVg deals with the matter by supplying commas: _est autem Hierosolymis, super Probatica, piscina_. – Michael Metlen: The Vulgate Gospels as a Translation (continued). _Catholic Biblical Quarterly_ 9 (1947) 106–110, at p. 109.
This verse is missing in the Weber/Gryson edition and in NVg. The Clementina adds the folkloric story about the angel who moves the water.
